chapters.title: Chapter 323 | Asuranti II
paragraphs: Dexter nodded.
The mysterious connection had spared him the terror of Asuranti’s wail, but it did not spare him the weight of the Divine General’s presence.
His back bent slightly, and the stones beneath his boots cracked as, for a moment, he felt as though an enormous hand had settled between his shoulders and was trying to push him into the floor.
The Asura Slaughter Demon Body stirred, his muscles tightened, and his spine slowly straightened as he stood up.

Cole looked at him in astonishment, but Dexter barely noticed. He was looking upward, and through the broken roof he could see crimson light staining the sky as golden light flashed across it when Director Rourke moved to intercept the summoned being. Another impact followed.
"BAAAANG!"
The building shuddered, and Dexter’s gaze hardened.
"Everyone," he said, "we need to find a way out."
Blitz swallowed.
"We tried the barrier."
"Then we try something else."
Dexter turned.
The portal keeper lay near the broken formation posts, trembling beneath the pressure, his face pale.
Yet when Dexter looked at him, the man’s mouth slowly curved, and that smile settled the matter. Dexter crossed the floor, seized the villain by the throat, and lifted his upper body from the ground.
"Get us the fuck out of here."
His voice was low, and the prisoner looked into his eyes, then laughed. It was an unpleasant sound through his broken mouth.
"Out?"
Dexter’s fingers tightened, and the man’s laugh became a rasp.
"There’s no way out for you."
He looked toward the red light above the ruined roof.
"The sacrifice has been made. It has been summoned."
His expression twisted into something almost reverent.
"Forget this facility. All of Stargate City is doomed!"
"Hahaha!"

Dexter stared at him and did not believe that for a moment. Stargate City contained people far more powerful than this idiot understood. The nine families did not hold their positions merely because they possessed money, and the Hero Association had not spread across the continent by hiding whenever a dangerous creature appeared. Dexter had seen enough of his own neighborhood to know that appearances meant very little. A Transcendent life-form was terrifying, but it was not automatically the end of the city. Unfortunately, that distinction did nothing for the people trapped inside the formation.
Dexter lowered his voice.
"You were moving people through a portal."
The prisoner’s smile thinned.
"You don’t know where it led."
"Then you can explain."
"I don’t think I will."
Dexter studied him for a moment, then looked toward his squad.
"The situation is getting worse. He knows something about moving through this formation, and he won’t help willingly."
Cole’s expression tightened, and Dexter looked back at the prisoner.
"We may have to torture it out of him."

The word changed the room. Blitz looked at Cole, Gridlock’s hands went still, and even Bullet Spear Man shifted his gaze toward Dexter. The men had killed today, repeatedly, in open combat with enemies trying to cut them apart, but this was different. The prisoner could no longer stand, and his weapons had been taken.
Cole forced himself upright and approached. The pressure made every step difficult, but he reached Dexter and placed a hand against his arm.
"Dexter."
Dexter did not release the prisoner.
"We’re heroes," Cole said quietly. "Members of the Hero Association. If we torture someone who’s already helpless, we’re stepping onto the same road as them."
The villain watched the exchange with obvious interest, and Dexter’s jaw tightened.
"Do you think he’ll help if we ask nicely?"
"No. But—"
"Look behind you."
Cole did not turn, because he already knew what Dexter meant: the rescued captives, the injured, the people struggling to breathe beneath Asuranti’s pressure.
"If we stay here and that thing reaches us, we may not have time for another conversation," Dexter said. "He’s the only person we have who can open a portal."
"We don’t even know whether he can take us outside."
"Then that’s another answer we need."

Cole’s hand remained on his arm, and for several seconds the two men looked at each other. Neither was pretending the choice was simple. Finally, Dexter looked back at the prisoner, and his left hand opened.
"FWOOSH!"

A flame appeared above his palm. Blood red burned at its center, violet surrounded it, and along the outer edge a thin white light flickered with an intensity that made the nearby shadows retreat. The portal keeper stopped smiling, not entirely, but enough for Dexter to notice.
"Create the portal," Dexter said. "Give us a way out, or find out how long you can keep refusing."
The man looked at the flame, then at Dexter, and slowly his grin returned.
"Pain?"
He shook his head.
"You think pain will make me obey you?"
Dexter said nothing, and the villain’s eyes brightened with a sudden, ugly pride.
"Do you have any idea what I endured to obtain this talent?"
Cole’s brows drew together, and the prisoner continued.
"I was born with an E-rank mana affinity."
His voice became louder.
"E-rank. Do you know what people told me? That I should be grateful if I ever became useful carrying supplies for real cultivators."
His breathing quickened.
"They laughed when I spoke about entering a gate. They laughed when I asked for a proper cultivation method."
Dexter’s expression did not change, and the man leaned forward against the grip at his throat.
"Then someone offered me a chance."
A distant boom shook dust from the ceiling, but the prisoner ignored it.
"I was changed. Rebuilt. Reborn."
His gaze moved across the squad, daring them to dismiss him.
"My affinity rose to C-rank, and I was given a C-rank portal-creation talent."

Gridlock looked sharply at Cole. An acquired talent and an increased mana affinity: the implications were larger than the man seemed to realize, or perhaps he realized them perfectly and enjoyed watching their faces.
Others died," he said, and his grin widened. "They screamed until they couldn’t scream anymore. They begged for it to stop."
Dexter watched him closely. The man’s pride was real, and so was the memory behind it.
"But I..."
His voice rose.
"I survived!"
He struck his fist weakly against his own chest.
"I endured what they couldn’t. I stayed alive when stronger men broke. I earned this power."
He looked at Dexter’s flame again.
"You want to break me with pain?"
A hoarse laugh escaped him.
"Dream on. Let’s see how long it takes before you get tired of trying."
Nobody spoke immediately as they gazed at him with astonishment. It was shocking just how much he had suffered.

paragraphs: "I must say," Dexter said quietly, "I’m impressed."
The prisoner frowned as he looked at Dexter skeptically.
"I was born with a low mana affinity too."
Dexter tilted his head slightly.
"I simply never received an invitation to join the Villain Association."
The man frowned and studied Dexter’s face more carefully. Recognition moved through his expression, then disbelief followed it.
"Y-you..."
Dexter waited.
"You’re Dexter, Dexter Ashford. The bastard son."

Cole’s hand fell from Dexter’s arm, and the prisoner stared. Then his eyes shifted toward the bloodstained saber at Dexter’s side, toward the bodies of the men Dexter had killed, and his face changed.
"No."
The word escaped before he seemed to realize he had spoken.
"No, that’s impossible."
Dexter watched him.
"I heard you had an F-rank affinity and no talent. Nothing."
The man shook his head.
"You shouldn’t even be able to stand under this pressure."
His breathing became uneven.
"Those men were Ultra Realm cultivators. You shouldn’t have been able to kill them so easily."
Dexter smiled faintly, and the prisoner’s eyes moved over him again in disbelief.
"Impossible," he muttered. "That’s impossible."
"Would you like to know how I did it?"
The man went still, and for a moment his attention sharpened so completely that even Asuranti’s pressure seemed to disappear from his awareness. Then suspicion returned.
"You think you can tempt me into helping you?"
Dexter shrugged, lowered the man to the floor, and released his throat.
"It’s your choice."
The flame remained above his left palm, and the prisoner rubbed his bruised neck. His gaze shifted toward the squad: Cole, Gridlock, Blitz still leaning against the support, then back to Dexter.
"If you could pass it on, you would already have given it to your squad."
Dexter glanced at his companions, his expression unreadable, then looked back at the prisoner.
"If it were you, would you reveal an opportunity like that to everyone around you?"
The villain said nothing.
"If we weren’t trapped here with something that could kill us at any moment, do you think we would be having this conversation?"

The prisoner’s eyes narrowed. That answer made sense to him, l. A person who possessed a method capable of overturning his fate would guard it, keep it, and use it to climb above everyone who had once looked down on him.
The villain looked at Dexter’s face again: F-rank affinity, no talent, now strong enough to kill Ultra hero experts as a Superhuman hero.
He wanted the explanation, and Dexter could see that desire taking hold. For several seconds the man remained silent, then he swallowed.
"Fine."
Cole’s gaze sharpened, and the prisoner raised one finger.
"But you give me a hint first."
Dexter looked down at him.
The man gritted his teeth as he continued. "Proof for me to know you aren’t lying."
For a moment Dexter considered it.
A fragment of a seventh-tier cultivation method would be enough to make the man believe that an extraordinary opportunity existed and enough tj make him cooperate.
But Dexter’s eyes suddenly cooled, and the flame in his palm brightened. The prisoner noticed, and his expression faltered.
"Wait. I said—"
"Fuck that."
Dexter’s palm struck his chest.
"PAH!"

The man’s chest compressed inside slightly but the shocking part was how the flames in Dexter hand didn’t spread out like flames but Instead, a soft violet light appeared beneath his chest, and the glow sank inward. Like water soaking into dry cloth, the flame disappeared into him, and the prisoner sucked in a breath. His body stiffened, then he glared at Dexter.
"I knew you were lying. Even with your flames, there’s no way I’ll—"

His voice stopped as a violent chill passed through his chest. He looked down: the violet glow had already faded from the surface, but something moved inside him, cold, then heat, then both at once. His hands clenched against the floor.
"W-what sort of flame is this?"

Dexter withdrew his palm. The Abyssal Heavenly Flame did not consume the man’s flesh, and it did not burn his soul. It touched his mana and followed it. The prisoner’s breath caught as the sensation spread through every part of his body that his energy reached. It felt as though he had been plunged into a frozen lake while a furnace burned beneath his ribs. His back arched, and a groan escaped him before he forced his teeth together. No, he had survived worse. That was what he told himself: he had endured the procedure that changed his affinity, he had watched others die beside him, and he had remained. His fingers dug against the stone, and he would remain now.
Dexter watched his face. The man’s will was strong, but he had mistaken the first sensation for the full nature of the flame.
The heat and cold were only what his body could understand; the rest reached deeper into perception and memory,
For one instant the prisoner still saw the entire hall, Dexter standing above him, Cole beside the platform, the broken roof.
Then in thag split second, the room vanished. In his awareness something vast opened beneath him as darkness surged and he fell into the 11th pit of hell.
The place that had concept of time. He felt himself fall, and the shapes waiting below lifted their heads.
The demons caught him and the first round of torture truly began.
Outside that nightmare, one second passed. Inside it, a year went by slowly.
"AHHHHHHHHH!"
The scream struck the walls, and Cole flinched and the others flinched in shock.
The man rolled and thrashed around the floor, like he was dying, no longer trying to preserve his pride, and his voice rose sharply, cracked, and became a ragged rasp.
"AAARGH—!"
Blood vessels stood out along his neck, his hands shook, and a thin red trace slipped from the corner of one eye. Blitz stared.
"What did you do?"
Dexter did not answer as he continued to look at the man coldly.
The man who had boasted of endurance could no longer remember why he had believed this would resemble the pain he knew.
Another second began, and his scream intensified. His eyes flew wide as he saw Dexter.
"Please!"
The word tore out of him, and the others went still. There was no defiance left in his face, no pride, only a desperate effort to hold on to the sight of the man standing above him.
"Please, I’ll do it!"
His voice broke.
"Let me do it!"

chapters.title: Chapter 325 | Asuranti’s Attack
paragraphs: "GET ME OUT OF HERE!"
"Dexter... he might really die from shock." Cole stammered.
Dexter’s expression remained cold but then he sighed and then, he raised his left hand and slapped at the villain’s chest.
"PAH!"

A violet glow spread beneath the man’s skin, and then the flame withdrew. Thin strands of blood-red fire, edged in violet and white, streamed from his chest into Dexter’s palm, twisting together for an instant before disappearing between his fingers.
The screaming stopped, and the villain fell sideways.
"Haaah! Haaah! Haaah!"

He dragged air into his lungs as though he had been drowning, and his entire body trembled. For several moments his eyes remained open without focusing on anything: the floor, the broken platform, the ruined ceiling. He looked at each of them with desperate confusion, struggling to understand where he was, and then his gaze found Dexter.
"AHHH!"
He jerked backward, his flesh scraping against the stone and turning bloody as he tried to drag himself away.
"Don’t!"
Dexter had not moved, but the villain curled inward anyway, raising both arms over his head.
"Don’t come here!"
His voice was cracked.
"Please. I’ll do it. I’ll do anything. Just don’t come close."
Cole stared at him. Two seconds was all it had taken.
The man who had proudly declared that no amount of pain could break him was now shaking so violently that his teeth clicked together.

Blitz swallowed, and Gridlock looked from the prisoner to Dexter’s empty hand. Nobody asked what the flame had made him experience, and from the way he kept looking at things that were not there, they were not certain they wanted to know.
Dexter lowered his hand.
"The portal."
The villain flinched at his voice.
"Yes. Yes!"
He raised one trembling arm, and silver lines flickered beneath his skin. For a moment nothing happened, and his face twisted in panic.
"Wait! Please, just—"
Space rippled.
"Woooooom!"

A pale violet point appeared several steps away, stretched upward, then widened into an oval as the ruined loading hall seemed to fold around its edges. Dexter’s eyes sharpened. Through the opening he saw sunlight, real sunlight, not the crimson glow beneath the Nine Hell Chain Formation. A street lay beyond the portal, with vehicles abandoned along its edges and people crowded behind temporary barricades, staring toward the enormous black dome covering the training center. Several heroes stood closer to the barrier, some examining it and others arguing into communication devices.
The villain’s hand shook harder.
"There," he whispered. "Outside. It’s outside."

Dexter looked at the scene beyond the opening. So the man really had possessed a way through. Whatever permission, anchor, or exception his talent used, the formation had allowed him to create a passage, and the restriction that had stopped everyone else had not stopped him. Dexter’s jaw tightened as someone outside noticed the portal. A woman holding a phone stumbled backward.
"What’s that?"
The violet opening expanded, and someone screamed.
"RUN!"
The crowd broke.
"It’s another gate!"
"Monster outbreak!"
"GET BACK!"

People scattered from the barricade. A man abandoned his bag, someone fell and scrambled upright before running on, and several heroes moved in the opposite direction. A woman carrying a long sword planted herself directly in front of the portal, two others spread to either side of her, mana gathered, a bowstring tightened, and the point of a spear lowered toward the opening. Dexter did not blame them, because if a portal had suddenly appeared beside a sealed disaster site, he would have prepared to attack too.
He turned toward his squad.
"All right. Let’s go."

For a moment nobody moved, they were obviously still stunned but when Dexter looked at them, Blitz straightened almost too quickly. Dexter noticed, but he said nothing. There would be time for that later, if they survived.
Cole drew a breath, then stepped toward the portal with both hands visible.
"Registered heroes!" he shouted. "We have injured survivors!"
The woman outside raised her sword slightly.
"Identify yourself!"
"Cole Stanley! Plasmatic Man! Don’t attack!"
He crossed, and for one tense instant every weapon outside remained pointed at him. Then a man behind the barricade recognized him.
"He’s registered! Let him through!"
Cole immediately turned back.
"Bring them!"
Burke lifted the nearest injured captive, Gridlock and Blitz supported two more between them, and Bullet Spear Man went next, keeping his weapon lowered while watching the heroes outside.

One by one the rescued captives disappeared into the daylight. The woman with the sword called for medical staff, someone outside began shouting that there were survivors inside the dome, and more heroes hurried toward the opening.
Dexter remained on the ruined side, watching until the last captive was clear, then looked down at the portal keeper. The man immediately recoiled.
"Please—"
"I’m not using the flame."

The prisoner’s eyes filled with fresh terror anyway, and Dexter grabbed the back of his clothing and lifted him. The villain kept his hand extended toward the portal, maintaining the spatial passage even as his body shook.
"Don’t close it."
"I-I won’t!"
Dexter moved toward the opening. He had only taken two steps forward, when literal death touched his back.
There was no warning. One moment he was approaching the portal, and the next a horrifying sensation wrapped around him: Death, straight up.
Every instinct in his body screamed, and Dexter’s face changed. ’Behind me!’ He tried to turn, but his reaction peed was too slow. He was like a bike racing against a race car!
"Flame Demon Transformation!"
"BOOOOOOM!"
Power erupted through his bloodline, and the flames did not spread across the floor but collapsed inward, wrapping around his body and pressing into his skin.

Demonic markings blazed across his arms, his hair lifted with violet-white fire flickering between the strands, and his eyes brightened as the force of the Abyssal Emperor Flame Demon Bloodline surged through his physique. The stone beneath his boots cracked as a 30 meter radius hole appared in the ground and his strength rose violently, but the danger did not weaken as it grew evencloser.
"Scorching Fury!"
"FWOOSH!"

sentences.text: "GET ME OUT OF HERE!"
"Dexter... he might really die from shock." Cole stammered.
Dexter’s expression remained cold but then he sighed and then, he raised his left hand and slapped at the villain’s chest.
"PAH!"
A violet glow spread beneath the man’s skin, and then the flame withdrew.
Thin strands of blood-red fire, edged in violet and white, streamed from his chest into Dexter’s palm, twisting together for an instant before disappearing between his fingers.
The screaming stopped, and the villain fell sideways.
"Haaah!
Haaah!
Haaah!"
He dragged air into his lungs as though he had been drowning, and his entire body trembled.
For several moments his eyes remained open without focusing on anything: the floor, the broken platform, the ruined ceiling.
He looked at each of them with desperate confusion, struggling to understand where he was, and then his gaze found Dexter.
"AHHH!"
He jerked backward, his flesh scraping against the stone and turning bloody as he tried to drag himself away.
"Don’t!"
Dexter had not moved, but the villain curled inward anyway, raising both arms over his head.
"Don’t come here!"
His voice was cracked.
"Please.
I’ll do it.
I’ll do anything.
Just don’t come close."
Cole stared at him.
Two seconds was all it had taken.
The man who had proudly declared that no amount of pain could break him was now shaking so violently that his teeth clicked together.
Blitz swallowed, and Gridlock looked from the prisoner to Dexter’s empty hand.
Nobody asked what the flame had made him experience, and from the way he kept looking at things that were not there, they were not certain they wanted to know.
Dexter lowered his hand.
"The portal."
The villain flinched at his voice.
"Yes.
Yes!"
He raised one trembling arm, and silver lines flickered beneath his skin.
For a moment nothing happened, and his face twisted in panic.
"Wait!
Please, just—"
Space rippled.
"Woooooom!"
A pale violet point appeared several steps away, stretched upward, then widened into an oval as the ruined loading hall seemed to fold around its edges.
Dexter’s eyes sharpened.
Through the opening he saw sunlight, real sunlight, not the crimson glow beneath the Nine Hell Chain Formation.
A street lay beyond the portal, with vehicles abandoned along its edges and people crowded behind temporary barricades, staring toward the enormous black dome covering the training center.
Several heroes stood closer to the barrier, some examining it and others arguing into communication devices.
The villain’s hand shook harder.
"There," he whispered.
"Outside.
It’s outside."
Dexter looked at the scene beyond the opening.
So the man really had possessed a way through.
Whatever permission, anchor, or exception his talent used, the formation had allowed him to create a passage, and the restriction that had stopped everyone else had not stopped him.
Dexter’s jaw tightened as someone outside noticed the portal.
A woman holding a phone stumbled backward.
"What’s that?"
The violet opening expanded, and someone screamed.
"RUN!"
The crowd broke.
"It’s another gate!"
"Monster outbreak!"
"GET BACK!"
People scattered from the barricade.
A man abandoned his bag, someone fell and scrambled upright before running on, and several heroes moved in the opposite direction.

A woman carrying a long sword planted herself directly in front of the portal, two others spread to either side of her, mana gathered, a bowstring tightened, and the point of a spear lowered toward the opening.
Dexter did not blame them, because if a portal had suddenly appeared beside a sealed disaster site, he would have prepared to attack too.
He turned toward his squad.
"All right.
Let’s go."
For a moment nobody moved, they were obviously still stunned but when Dexter looked at them, Blitz straightened almost too quickly.
Dexter noticed, but he said nothing.
There would be time for that later, if they survived.
Cole drew a breath, then stepped toward the portal with both hands visible.
"Registered heroes!" he shouted.
"We have injured survivors!"
The woman outside raised her sword slightly.
"Identify yourself!"
"Cole Stanley!
Plasmatic Man!
Don’t attack!"
He crossed, and for one tense instant every weapon outside remained pointed at him.
Then a man behind the barricade recognized him.
"He’s registered!
Let him through!"
Cole immediately turned back.
"Bring them!"
Burke lifted the nearest injured captive, Gridlock and Blitz supported two more between them, and Bullet Spear Man went next, keeping his weapon lowered while watching the heroes outside.
One by one the rescued captives disappeared into the daylight.
The woman with the sword called for medical staff, someone outside began shouting that there were survivors inside the dome, and more heroes hurried toward the opening.

The man immediately recoiled.
"Please—"
"I’m not using the flame."
The prisoner’s eyes filled with fresh terror anyway, and Dexter grabbed the back of his clothing and lifted him.
The villain kept his hand extended toward the portal, maintaining the spatial passage even as his body shook.
"Don’t close it."
"I-I won’t!"
Dexter moved toward the opening.
He had only taken two steps forward, when literal death touched his back.
There was no warning.
One moment he was approaching the portal, and the next a horrifying sensation wrapped around him: Death, straight up.
Every instinct in his body screamed, and Dexter’s face changed. ’Behind me!’ He tried to turn, but his reaction peed was too slow.
He was like a bike racing against a race car!
"Flame Demon Transformation!"
"BOOOOOOM!"
Power erupted through his bloodline, and the flames did not spread across the floor but collapsed inward, wrapping around his body and pressing into his skin.

Demonic markings blazed across his arms, his hair lifted with violet-white fire flickering between the strands, and his eyes brightened as the force of the Abyssal Emperor Flame Demon Bloodline surged through his physique.
The stone beneath his boots cracked as a 30 meter radius hole appared in the ground and his strength rose violently, but the danger did not weaken as it grew evencloser.
"Scorching Fury!"
"FWOOSH!"

chapters.title: Chapter 326 | Half-Step Transcendant Strength!
paragraphs: "BOOOM!"
Another powerful surge tore through Dexter, as the bloodline skill increase his strength by 80%!
His muscles tightened, as intense uncontrollable heat burst from his shoulders, and his strength climbed rapidly, pushing hard against the limits of the Ultra Realm!
Dexter gritted his teeth as he clenched the Void Star Saber tightly.
’Too slow! Still too slow.’
He had not even turned completely and the attack was approaching him at speed surprising supersonic!
At this realm, his body could barely comprehend such speed!
’What do I do?’
His heart slammed against his ribs.
’What do I do?!’
The portal was directly in front of him, Cole was on the other side, and safety was one step away, yet that single step might as well have been an ocean.

Dexter knew it. If the attack landed before he turned, he would die. Even with his present combat power almost breaking the boundary of Peak Ultra, he could feel how completely the incoming force exceeded what he could withstand.
For one terrible instant, panic threatened to swallow his thoughts. His wives appeared in his mind: Mira’s smirk, Lyra cute smile, and Selene’s gentle look.
He had promised them he would be safe, promised them he wouldn’t be injured, promised them this outing was nothing dangerous and yet... he had broken his promise!
’Think!’
’Wait, the system.’

His mind reached for it, but what was he expecting? For the system to step out of his body and stop the attack? It was not a guardian standing behind him, and it could not simply decide he was strong enough and make the danger disappear. Unless—
Dexter’s thoughts caught on something: a notification, the reward he got from the system and had forgotten due to various distractions which definitely had to do with his wives.
Ten years of cultivation!
Right!
The golden text immediately appared before him.
[PRIMARY REWARD TWO]
[Recognized Investment]
? Devoting personal time to the well-being and happiness of all three wives.
[Reward]
? Natural Lifespan Extension: 50 Years
? Compressed Cultivation: 10 Years
[Do you wish to accept reward? Yes or No!?]
There was no time for hesitation as he immediately roared in his mind.
’Accept!’
[Ding! Stored Cultivation Reward]
[Ten Years of Cultivation — Accepted]
"THUM!"
Something exploded deep within Dexter’s inner universe.
Years of accumulation, years of refining, stabilizing, and advancing, all compressed into a single overwhelming instant.
His inner universe blazed like a dying sun, and the vast cosmic DNA helix suspended within it began spinning as light raced through its awakened segments.
The next dark section trembled, cracked, then ignited, and the eleventh segment shone. Before its light could settle, the final segment began shaking.
"CRACK!"
Its dim outer shell broke apart, and radiance poured through it.
All twelve segments of the cosmic helix burned together, and Dexter felt the completed structure resonate through every part of his body.
Then all of a sudden, it compressed.
"Boom!"

Dexter’s body jolted as the long, twisting helix drew inward, its luminous sections pressing toward a single point and folding around one another under a pressure that made his inner universe tremble.
For an instant the structure resembled a tightly closed flower, then it became smaller and denser, and a seed started to from at its center.
The seed of a mandala flower hung within the darkness of his inner universe, as its surface marked with intricate lines that shifted as mana passed beneath them.
Dexter had no time to admire it, because the cultivation reward continued flowing. Across the vast space around the seed, dormant Star Nodes ignited one after another.
"THUM! THUM! THUM!"
Light spread through the darkness, and each awakened node gathered its own immense reservoir of mana.
The stars brightened, their gravity strengthened, and the inner universe that had once seemed mostly empty became filled with burning points of power.
The mandala seed pulsed, and thin almost translucent roots emerged from beneath it, then stretched outward across the darkness toward the surrounding stars.

One root reached a Star Node, and light rushed through it. Another found its connection, then another. One hundred and three roots spread beneath the seed, one hundred and three Star Nodes answered, and the entire structure came alive.
"RUMBLEEEEEEEEE!"
Dexter’s aura erupted. The floor beneath him sank, broken stones lifted into the air, and the portal rippled violently. Outside, Cole’s expression changed.
"Dexter!"
He had barely begun saying the name.
Everything inside Dexter’s inner universe had occurred within the smallest fraction of that cry.
The transformation was still active, Scorching Fury still surged through his blood, and now the foundation beneath both had changed.
His cultivation crossed into the Ultra Realm, and the newly formed mandala seed drew upon the power of one hundred and three stars, feeding his body with a force it had never possessed before.
Combined with his bloodline and body techniques, his combat aura surged beyond the level it had reached moments earlier, toward Half-Step Transcendent power.

The difference struck him immediately. The portal’s flickering edges became clearer, the dust hanging beside his face seemed to slow, and the terrible sensation behind him remained, but right now, he could finally react to thag speed!
Dexter moved as his left arm thrust the prisoner toward the portal, his right tightened around the saber, and he turned.
"Thunder GodKill Saber Art..."
Lightning exploded along the weapon.
"CRACKLE! CRACKLE!"
Eight currents formed almost at once, each drawing power from the stars burning within him, and the blade hummed violently. But Dexter was not finished.

The Abyssal Heavenly Flame poured from his bloodline, blood red at its heart, violet around it, and white along its outer edge, and the flame wrapped around the lightning. The two elements didn’t dare to repel each other as though knowing the danger which was coming.
"KRA-BOOM!!!"
Fire followed the shape of thunder, thunder carried the devouring force of the flame, and a new and devastating element appeared!
Dark lightning stroke the edge of the Void Star Saber as its black-violet body threaded with blood-red light shone like the maw of a heavenly demon.
The air around the weapon twisted, and Dexter could feel the immense strain in his arm, but he did not loosen his grip.
"Third Move..."

chapters.title: Chapter 327 | The Strong!
paragraphs: The air around the weapon twisted, and Dexter could feel the immense strain in his arm, but he did not loosen his grip.
"Third Move..."
With the immense power flowing through his veins, Dexter completed the turn.
However, there was nothing behind him. But the sensation of death remained and Dexter didn’t hesitate.
"Eifhtfold Lightning Severance!"
He immediately slashed outward.
"SHRRRRRIIIIIIING!"
Eight arcs of dark lightning tore from the blade, crossing one another in the air while wrapped in heavenly flame.
The void trembled, and space warped around their edges. For one split second, it seemed Dexter had gone mad and had simply struck at the air.
But in that instant, the air warped as a massive fist appeared!
First was the killing intent that enveloped Dexter and now, the gist dollars that killing intent!
The fused thunder and flame struck the knuckles, white light burst between them, and the space around the collision folded inward.
"KA—BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!"
The entire hall exploded as a massive shock wave tore through the building, ripping the remaining roof upward and blasting the shattered walls outward.
Dark lightning flashed through the rising dust, violet-white flames surged toward the sky, the ground beneath Dexter broke open, and the roar of the collision swallowed everything.
Just as Dexter blocked the fist, another tore through the air, intending to burst his head like a water melon pressed by a tank!
Dexter reacted quickly but there was not enough force in his attack as his blade struck the fist.
"Boom!"
The flat side of his blade pressed against his chest and Dexter felt ws though he had been hit by a moving high speed missile!
"Boom!"
His body blasted backwards and he was sent flying, crashing through the wall of a training house with a loud "BANG!"
Bricks and concrete followed him into the next room, but his body had already passed through the opposite wall.
"BANG! BANG!"
The second house collapsed around him, then the third, and dust filled his mouth as his vision shook and a sharp pain spread from his chest to his back.
Dexter gritted his teeth. Before he could crash into another building, he twisted his waist and forced his legs beneath him. His boots struck the street.
"SKRRRRRRRR!"
The ground tore open, and two deep trenches stretched behind his heels as he dragged across the concrete.
Broken stones piled against his legs before bursting apart under the force.
He immediately thrust his saber downward. The blade, carving another line between the trenches, but even then he could not immediately stop.
’What terrifying strength!’
His arms were numb.

He had already activated Flame Demon Transformation and Scorching Fury, his cultivation had broken through, and his one hundred and three Star Nodes were pouring mana through his body, yet a single punch had sent him through three houses. Dexter raised his head as the dust ahead suddenly parted.
"BOOM!"

Asuranti shot toward him like a bullet. Its enormous body crossed the ruined street in a flash, its feet barely touching the ground, and the pressure arriving ahead of it shoved the drifting dust into a solid-looking wall. Dexter’s pupils contracted.
’So fast!’

He had not even regained his footing. Asuranti drew back its fist, the crimson plates around its forearm tightened, and then it punched. Dexter ripped his saber from the ground and brought it across his body, pressing his left palm against the flat of the blade.
"CLAAAAANG!"

The impact rang through the entire street, and Dexter’s feet left the ground again. This time he flew so quickly that the buildings on either side blurred into dark streaks, and the barrier rushed toward him.
"BOOOOOOM!"
His back struck its shadowy surface.
"Ugh!"
Black ripples spread outward, enormous chain patterns flashed beneath the barrier, and the force rebounded through his body. Dexter coughed out a mouthful of blood, and his grip almost loosened.

Before he could fall, a shadow covered him. Asuranti was already there, its crimson eyes looking down at him, and the creature raised its fist and punched directly at his skull. Dexter tried to lift his saber, but his trembling arms barely moved.
’Damn it! I really don’t want to use this!"
But before he could do anything...
"BANG!"
Golden light flashed between them as a sword struck the side of Asuranti’s fist and forced the attack away from Dexter’s head.
The fist slammed into the barrier beside him.
"Your opponent is me!"

Director Rourke stepped into the narrow space before Dexter. His gym clothes were torn, and blood stained one side of his face, but the sword in his hand blazed with a fierce golden light. He turned his wrist, and the blade swept upward beneath Asuranti’s arm.
"BOOM!"
Golden sword light burst against the creature’s shoulder, and General Asuranti shifted a step backward.
Dexter manipulated mana into his legs.
"Flame Burst Step!"
He disappeared in a burst of violet-white fire, and a moment later Asuranti’s other hand swept through the place where he had been.
"WHOOOOSH!"
The wind from the strike ripped a long trench across the street.

Rourke retreated in the opposite direction and landed on the remains of a broken staircase, while Dexter landed several meters away. For an instant the two men looked at each other across the creature.
"Can you still fight?" Rourke asked.
Dexter wiped his mouth.
"Do I have a choice?"
The director’s lips twitched.
"No."
"Then I can."
Asuranti turned toward Dexter, and Rourke immediately moved.
His sword cut downward, releasing a golden crescent toward the creature’s neck, and at the same moment Dexter lowered his body and rushed toward its legs.
They attacked from different heights, and Asuranti raised an arm to block Rourke’s sword while Dexter’s saber flashed beneath it.
"Eightfold Lightning Severance!"
Eight streaks of dark lightning struck the same knee.
"CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!"
The first blows scattered against its armor, but the later ones found the narrow space between two overlapping plates, and Asuranti’s leg bent. Rourke’s eyes sharpened.
He stepped forward through the air and drove his sword toward the creature’s exposed throat.
"BOOOOOOM!"

paragraphs: The golden attack forced Asuranti back, and Dexter immediately changed position.
He moved behind its bent leg, dragging his saber across the back of its knee while heavenly flame streamed along the blade.
A thin crack appeared in the armor.
’It worked!’
Before he could press the advantage, Asuranti stamped down. Dexter kicked off the ground.
"BANG!"

"He’s growing stronger."
He tightened his grip on his sword.
"We won’t be able to stop him at all."
Dexter swallowed.
They had been trying to discover its weaknesses, but while they fought, it had been learning theirs.
Worse, it wa adapting and ufs strength was climbing too. If this continued, even surviving a single exchange would become impossible. His thoughts raced.
The portal remained their only way out, but with Asuranti moving at this speed, turning their backs on it would be no different from offering it their lives.

Asuranti charged again, and Rourke met it with a golden sword formation attack..
"BANG!"
Cracks spread across the tows of golden sword , and Dexter rushed to his side and struck the creature’s wrist, helping him turn the blow away.
"Director, I have an idea!"

paragraphs: "Really? What do I have to do?"
The man said with a grim face.
Dexter face hardened as he spoke quickly.
"Hold him back for five seconds."
Rourke glanced at him.
"Five seconds?"
"I’ll release my ultimate attack. Then we secure the villain who created the portal and get out of here before this thing kills us."
The director looked toward the distant violet light flickering through the ruins, then back at Dexter. The young man’s face was pale, but his gaze remained firm. Rourke nodded.
"You’re a brave hero."
He stepped in front of Dexter.
"Alright. We’ll do as you say."
Dexter immediately retreated, and his attention entered his storage ring.
The necklace appeared in his palm: Virgo’s Might, a single stored attack carrying the power of a Peak Transcendent expert. His fingers closed around it. Dexter immediately drove his mana into it.
"BZZZZZZ!"
The pendant trembled, and a faint light appeared beneath its surface. At the same moment, Rourke raised his sword.
Every trace of golden light around him rushed toward the blade, and his aura climbed violently as the ground beneath his feet cracked.
"Heaven Judgment!"
His voice thundered across the ruins.
"Quad Godfall Sword Formation!"
"RUMMMMMBLE!"
Four enormous golden swords formed behind him.

The first rose above the surrounding buildings, the second was larger, the third stretched farther still, and the fourth towered over the others, its sharp edge pressing against the air until the entire street rang with a piercing hum. Rourke’s face drained of color.
He had poured almost everything he possessed into the formation, and his raised hand trembled before he brought it down.
"Fall!"
The first sword descended.
"WHOOOOOSH!"
Asuranti looked up and raised its fist.
"BAAAAAANG!"
The golden sword shattered against the punch, and thousands of brilliant fragments scattered across the street.
Rourke did not retreat, as he punched out. The second sword fell forward as Asuranti struck it again.
"BOOOOOOM!"

This time its arm sank slightly, its feet drove into the ground, and a thin crack appeared across the crimson armor covering its knuckles. The second sword broke, but the creature had stopped advancing. Behind Rourke, Dexter’s inner universe shook. Mana rushed through the roots beneath the mandala seed, and one Star Node dimmed, then another, then six more. Their light flowed toward the necklace in his hand, and Dexter’s fingers tightened.
’Faster!’
The third sword struck, and Asuranti brought both hands upward.
"BOOOOOOOOOOM!"

The ground beneath it collapsed, and the enormous golden blade pressed downward between its palms. Its arms trembled, and for the first time the creature could not immediately break the attack. Rourke roared, and the sword sank another few meters as Asuranti’s knees bent. One second passed, then a little more.
"CRAAAAACK!"

Golden fractures spread along the blade, and Asuranti pushed upward. The third sword burst apart, and the fourth descended through its shattered remains. The entire street turned golden, and even Dexter felt the pressure. He lowered his body, protecting the necklace against his chest as the shock wave struck.
"KA—BOOOOOOOOOOM!"

The final sword collided with Asuranti’s fists. Buildings shook, a row of broken walls collapsed, and the blast drove Dexter backward, his boots scraping two lines through the ground. But he did not loosen his grip. He forced more mana into the necklace, and inside his inner universe the stars continued going dark. Seventy. Fifty. Thirty. Their reservoirs emptied one after another, and the necklace grew heavier in his palm as the power sealed within it stirred.

Across the street, Asuranti struggled beneath the fourth sword. The armor covering both fists cracked, and its feet sank deeper. For a moment Rourke almost believed the attack would drive it into the ground, and then the creature raised its head. Its crimson eyes brightened.
"CRACK!"
One enormous fracture split the golden sword, and Rourke’s expression changed. Asuranti straightened.
"CRAAAAASH!"

The fourth sword exploded. Golden light swept across the ruins, Rourke staggered, and his sword dimmed. There was nothing left to put into another formation. Four seconds. He turned his head. Dexter was still standing behind him, both hands around the necklace. The pendant had begun to shine, but it was not ready. One second remained.

Asuranti stepped out of the shattered sword light, and its aura was even stronger. The pressure rolling from it made Rourke’s chest tighten, and it was approaching the peak of the Transcendent Realm. The director looked at Dexter once more, then gritted his teeth.
’One second.’
His legs bent, and the ground cracked beneath them.
"AAAAAH!"

Rourke hurled himself forward. There was no golden sword light around him, no shield, and no formation. He had exhausted his mana, and only the strength of his Half-Step Transcendent body remained. Asuranti turned toward him, and Rourke drew back his fist. The creature did the same, and their fists collided.
"BAAAAAANG!"
The sound struck Dexter’s ears like thunder. Rourke’s arm twisted, and his body shot backward.
"BANG!"
He smashed through a stone pillar.
"BANG! BANG!"
Two more burst apart behind him, and then he struck the ground.
"BOOOOOOM!"
A crater twenty meters in radius opened beneath his body, and dust rushed upward. Rourke lay at its center, blood spilling from the corner of his mouth, one arm bent at an unnatural angle.
"Director!"

Dexter’s heart shook. His instinct was to move, to reach him, but the necklace was still drawing mana. If he stopped now, the second Rourke had bought with his own body would be wasted. Dexter’s jaw clenched, and he forced the last remaining streams of mana into the pendant. Five Star Nodes dimmed, then three, then one. The light beneath the mandala seed flickered.
Asuranti turned, and its attention returned to Dexter. The creature took a step.
"BOOM!"

The ground behind it burst apart, and Dexter’s pupils shrank. It was already before him. The enormous hand opened, and long nails extended from its fingers as it reached toward his chest. Five inches. That was all that remained between those claws and his heart. Dexter could see the cracks in the crimson armor, feel the pressure pushing against his ribs, and he had no strength left to jump away. His saber would not rise in time.
’Charge!’
